requirement_text.REQ-063: Execute Decision 0006's D1: relocate users, groups and tenant_role from the public schema into each tenant's own Postgres schema via :prefix. Full design (approved through security + idiom gates): lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md. Acceptance criteria (from docs/requirements.yaml, verbatim): users/groups/tenant_role each exist inside at least two distinct provisioned tenant schemas (information_schema.tables check, and the same query false for public post-cutover); each of the three migrations carries the prefix()-truthiness guard (a plain mix ecto.migrate creates ZERO of the three tables in public); two users with the same username can be created in two different tenant schemas without conflict, a duplicate within one schema still conflicts; the same (external_realm, external_id) pair cannot be bound to two tenants (rejected by tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index); existing public rows are copied into the correct per-tenant schema before public tables drop, row-count equality plus a spot-check; AuthPipeline's full flow (token -> realm -> tenant -> per-schema user lookup/JIT provisioning) passes end to end against a per-tenant users table.

task.description:
ELIXIR-DEV's own full-suite run (Step 2a) reported 722/761 passing, 39 failing -- every failure confined to exactly two categories the design doc's own §7 item 4 predicted in advance (quoted here verbatim so you don't have to re-derive it): 'Every existing test that inserts a User/Group/TenantRole fixture directly (no prefix: option) currently lands in public... Test fixtures will need to insert into a real provisioned tenant schema (via TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/2) rather than the bare public table.' The two failure categories are (a) tests whose fixtures assume a public-schema users/groups/tenant_role table that no longer exists post-cutover, and (b) tests calling the old provision_oidc_user/3 arity, now /4. This is NOT a regression to diagnose -- it is the expected, designed consequence of the schema move, and your job is to update these ~39 tests' fixtures/call sites to the new per-tenant-schema reality, per the design's own guidance.

Read lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md in full, focused on §7 item 4's fixture guidance and §5b's provision_oidc_user/4 signature. Then: (1) update test/letflow/identity_test.exs and test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs's fixtures to provision a real tenant schema (TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/2, the same pattern req022 §3's testing-environment caveat already documents for Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox -- read that caveat before writing these tests, it flags a real sandbox-mode gotcha) rather than inserting into the bare public table; (2) update every provision_oidc_user/3 call site in tests to the new /4 arity with an explicit prefix; (3) run the full mix test suite yourself and confirm the 39 failures are gone with no new failures introduced elsewhere.

Beyond fixing the 39 pre-existing test breaks, write NEW tests covering acceptance criteria this run's own gates haven't already exercised end-to-end: the two per-tenant-vs-global unique-index behavior changes (username; external_realm+external_id) -- ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2a summary and SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c summary both did manual/exploratory verification of these against a live Docker Postgres, but that is not the same as a committed, repeatable ExUnit test asserting the behavior; the drop migration's guard-skip-on-uncopied-row behavior (ELIXIR-DEV empirically demonstrated this manually per their handoff -- turn it into a real test); and the full AuthPipeline token->realm->tenant->per-schema-user flow (acceptance criterion 6) if no existing test already covers it end to end.

Do NOT write tests for REQ-064's future scope (tenant_id column removal) -- that's out of scope for this run.
acceptance_criteria: All ~39 pre-existing test failures fixed (fixtures updated to real tenant-schema provisioning, provision_oidc_user call sites updated to /4), confirmed by re-running mix test yourself with real output quoted
No new test failures introduced by the fixture changes
A test exists asserting two users with the same username succeed in two different tenant schemas, and conflict within one schema
A test exists asserting the same (external_realm, external_id) cannot bind to two tenants (rejected by tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index)
A test exists exercising the drop migration's guard-skip behavior when a row is uncopied
A test exists exercising AuthPipeline's full token->realm->tenant->per-schema-user flow end to end
No test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, not shared hardcoded tenant/schema names
